reason: The text demonstrates God's favor toward the Hebrew people through multiple actions: (1) God rewards the midwives who fear Him and refuse to kill the Hebrew babies, (2) the narrative explicitly states 'וַיֵּ֥יטֶב אֱלֹהִ֖ים לַֽמְיַלְּדֹ֑ת' ('And God was good to the midwives'), (3) as a result, 'וַיִּ֧רֶב הָעָ֛ם וַיַּֽעַצְמ֖וּ מְאֹֽד' ('the people multiplied and became very mighty'), and (4) God makes houses for the midwives, establishing families. The theological narrative structure shows God blessing and preserving the Hebrew population through divine reward for those who protect Hebrew life, which strongly implies God's desire for their wellbeing and flourishing.
